usageNotes: Revokes the node's current ACME-issued TLS certificate with the CA (e.g., Let's Encrypt), which will invalidate the certificate in the CA's records and trigger a new certificate order if ACME is reconfigured. Use this when you need to permanently retire a certificate — such as when rotating ACME accounts, changing the domain, or responding to a compromise. Requires Sys.Modify on the node; the node must be reachable and the ACME plugin must already be configured.

examples.summary: Revoke the ACME certificate on node pve1

destructiveReason: Revokes the node's TLS certificate with the ACME CA, immediately invalidating it; the node will fall back to its self-signed certificate until a new ACME certificate is issued.
tips: After revocation the node's web UI and API will present a self-signed certificate, causing browser warnings and breaking clients that enforce certificate validation.
This does not delete the local certificate files — use the ACME order endpoint to issue a replacement after revocation.
Revocation is reported to the CA and cannot be undone; if you only need to renew, use the POST /acme/certificate endpoint instead.
